newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Violence-torn S.African gold mines peaceful on Wed.
newsitem.headline: Violence-torn S.African gold mines peaceful on Wed.

text.p: Peace has returned to the gold mining area southwest of Johannesburg where 21 people have been killed and 38 seriously injured in ethnic clashes since Saturday, police said on Wednesday.

The violence between members of the Sotho and Xhosa tribes have centred on the Buffelsfontein Gold Mining Company Ltd, owned by marginal mines specialist Randgold & Exploration Co Ltd, which recently bought it from Gencor Ltd.
"At this stage the situation has normalised. From Tuesday afternoon workers have been going down the shafts as scheduled," police Superintendant Pieter du Plessis said.

"Police are maintaining a presence and they will start with clean-up operations, searching the hostels for dangerous weapons and any other information that may help them in their investigations," du Plessis said.
In July and August some 30 miners were killed in ethnic clashes on four other mines, run by Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd.
President Nelson Mandela has appointed a judicial inquiry into the fighting.

Migrant labourers at most of the country's mines are accommodated in hostels segregated by ethnic group. Union leaders say the system is a legacy of apartheid but mine managers say the workers do not want to be forced to share housing with members of other tribes.
